subject: maths

concepts.title: Ordered Pairs
concepts.definition: An ordered pair consists of two elements grouped in a fixed order, written as (a, b), where a is the first element and b is the second element.
concepts.formula: (a, b) where a is first coordinate, b is second coordinate
concepts.key_idea: Order matters: (a, b) is not equal to (b, a) unless a equals b.
question_patterns: determine if the given ordered pairs are equal
find the values of x and y if the ordered pairs are equal
list the ordered pairs formed from the given sets
identify the first and second elements of the ordered pair
Explain the method of Ordered Pairs.

solution_steps.explain: Check if the first coordinates of both ordered pairs are equal.
Check if the second coordinates of both ordered pairs are equal.
The ordered pairs are equal only if both the first and second coordinates match exactly.

worked_examples.question: Are the ordered pairs (2, 3) and (3, 2) equal?
worked_examples.solution: Compare first elements: 2 is not equal to 3. Compare second elements: 3 is not equal to 2. Since the first coordinates differ, the pairs are not equal.

worked_examples.question: Find x and y if (x, 5) = (4, y).
worked_examples.solution: For ordered pairs to be equal, first elements must match and second elements must match. So x = 4 and y = 5.

exercises.question: Are the ordered pairs (1, 2) and (1, 2) equal?
Find x if (x, 7) = (9, 7).

concepts.title: Cartesian Product of Sets
concepts.definition: The Cartesian product of two non-empty sets A and B is the set of all ordered pairs (a, b) where a belongs to A and b belongs to B.
concepts.formula: A x B = {(a, b) : a in A and b in B}
concepts.key_idea: Every element of the first set is paired with every element of the second set.
question_patterns: find the Cartesian product A x B
write all ordered pairs in A x B
determine the elements of A cross B
list the Cartesian product of the given sets
Explain the method of Cartesian Product of Sets.

solution_steps.explain: Write down all distinct elements of the first set A.

solution_steps.action: pair each with elements of B
solution_steps.explain: For each element of A, form ordered pairs with every element of B.
Collect all ordered pairs inside braces to form A x B.

worked_examples.question: If A = {1, 2} and B = {3, 4}, find A x B.
worked_examples.solution: Pair each element of A with every element of B: (1,3), (1,4), (2,3), (2,4).

worked_examples.question: If A = {a, b} and B = {x, y, z}, find A x B.
worked_examples.solution: Pair each element of A with every element of B: (a,x), (a,y), (a,z), (b,x), (b,y), (b,z).

exercises.question: If A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {4, 5}, find A x B.
If P = {m, n} and Q = {p, q, r}, write P x Q.

concepts.title: Number of Elements in Cartesian Product
concepts.definition: The number of elements in the Cartesian product A x B equals the product of the number of elements in A and the number of elements in B.
concepts.key_idea: Cardinality of the product is the product of cardinalities.
question_patterns: find the number of elements in A x B
how many ordered pairs are in the Cartesian product
if n(A) and n(B) are given, find n(A x B)
determine the cardinality of the Cartesian product
Explain the method of Number of Elements in Cartesian Product.

solution_steps.explain: Determine the number of distinct elements in set A.
Determine the number of distinct elements in set B.
The number of ordered pairs in A x B is the product of the two counts.

worked_examples.question: If n(A) = 3 and n(B) = 4, find n(A x B).
worked_examples.solution: Using the formula n(A x B) = n(A) * n(B) = 3 * 4 = 12.

worked_examples.question: If A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {a, b}, find the number of elements in A x B.

exercises.question: If n(A) = 5 and n(B) = 7, find n(A x B).
If A x B has 20 elements and n(A) = 4, find n(B).

concepts.title: Definition of Relation, Domain, Codomain, Range
concepts.definition: A relation R from a set A to a set B is a subset of the Cartesian product A x B. The set of all first elements is the domain, the set B is the codomain, and the set of all second elements is the range.
concepts.formula: R subset A x B; Domain = {a : (a,b) in R}; Range = {b : (a,b) in R}
concepts.key_idea: A relation is any subset of the Cartesian product; domain is first elements, range is second elements, codomain is the whole target set.
question_patterns: find the domain and range of the given relation
determine if R is a relation from A to B
write the domain, codomain, and range of R
identify the relation as a subset of A x B
Explain the method of Definition of Relation, Domain, Codomain, Range.

solution_steps.explain: List all ordered pairs that belong to the relation R.
Collect all first elements for the domain and all second elements for the range.
The codomain is the entire set B to which the relation maps.

worked_examples.question: Let R = {(1, a), (2, b), (3, a)} be a relation from A = {1, 2, 3} to B = {a, b, c}. Find the domain and range.
worked_examples.solution: First elements: 1, 2, 3 form the domain. Second elements: a, b form the range. Codomain is B = {a, b, c}.
worked_examples.answer: Domain = {1, 2, 3}, Range = {a, b}, Codomain = {a, b, c}.

worked_examples.question: If R = {(x, y) : x in {1,2}, y in {3,4} and x + y is even}, find the domain and range.
worked_examples.solution: Check pairs: (1,3) sum 4 even, (1,4) sum 5 odd, (2,3) sum 5 odd, (2,4) sum 6 even. So R = {(1,3), (2,4)}. Domain = {1,2}, Range = {3,4}.

exercises.question: Let R = {(1, p), (2, q), (3, r)} from A to B. Find the domain and range.
If R = {(a, 1), (b, 2), (a, 3)}, find the domain and range.

concepts.title: Pictorial Diagrams of Relations
concepts.definition: A relation can be represented pictorially using arrow diagrams, where elements of A and B are placed in two regions and arrows link each first element to its corresponding second element.
concepts.formula: Arrow from a in A to b in B if (a, b) in R
concepts.key_idea: Arrows visually represent the mapping from domain elements to range elements.
question_patterns: draw the arrow diagram for the given relation
represent the relation pictorially
identify the relation from the arrow diagram
write the relation shown by the arrows
Explain the method of Pictorial Diagrams of Relations.

solution_steps.action: list elements of A and B
solution_steps.explain: Place the elements of set A on the left and elements of set B on the right.
For each ordered pair (a, b) in R, draw an arrow from a to b.
Confirm that every arrow corresponds to an ordered pair in the relation and no pair is missing.

worked_examples.question: Draw the arrow diagram for R = {(1, a), (2, b), (3, a)} from A = {1,2,3} to B = {a,b,c}.
worked_examples.solution: Place 1,2,3 on the left and a,b,c on the right. Draw arrows: 1 to a, 2 to b, 3 to a.

worked_examples.question: From an arrow diagram with arrows 1->x, 2->y, write the relation.
worked_examples.solution: Each arrow represents an ordered pair. So R = {(1, x), (2, y)}.

exercises.question: Draw the arrow diagram for R = {(a, 1), (b, 2), (c, 1)}.
Write the relation represented by arrows p->3, q->5.

concepts.title: Function as Special Type of Relation
concepts.definition: A function f from A to B is a relation where every element of A has exactly one image in B, meaning no element of A is left unmapped and no element of A maps to more than one element of B.
concepts.formula: f: A -> B such that for each a in A, there exists unique b in B with (a,b) in f
concepts.key_idea: Every input has exactly one output; no input is left without an image and no input has two images.
question_patterns: determine if the given relation is a function
check whether f is a function from A to B
justify why the relation is or is not a function
identify which relation represents a function
Explain the method of Function as Special Type of Relation.

solution_steps.explain: Verify that every element of A appears as a first element in the relation.
Verify that no element of A is paired with more than one element of B.
If both conditions hold, the relation is a function; otherwise it is not.

worked_examples.question: Is R = {(1, a), (2, b), (3, c)} a function from A = {1,2,3} to B = {a,b,c}?
worked_examples.solution: Every element of A (1, 2, 3) has exactly one image in B. No element maps to two values. So R is a function.

worked_examples.question: Is R = {(1, a), (1, b), (2, c)} a function from A = {1,2} to B = {a,b,c}?
worked_examples.solution: Element 1 maps to both a and b, violating the uniqueness condition. So R is not a function.
worked_examples.answer: No, R is not a function because 1 has two images.

exercises.question: Is R = {(1, p), (2, p), (3, p)} a function from A = {1,2,3} to B = {p,q}?
Is R = {(a, 1), (b, 2)} a function from A = {a,b,c} to B = {1,2,3}?

concepts.title: Domain, Codomain, Range of Functions
concepts.definition: For a function f: A -> B, the set A is the domain, the set B is the codomain, and the set of all images of elements of A is the range, which is a subset of the codomain.
concepts.formula: Domain = A, Codomain = B, Range = {f(x) : x in A} subset B
concepts.key_idea: The range is the actual set of output values, which is always contained within the codomain.
question_patterns: find the domain and range of the function
determine the range of f given its domain
identify the codomain of the function
state whether range equals codomain
Explain the method of Domain, Codomain, Range of Functions.

solution_steps.explain: The domain is the set of all inputs A for which f is defined.
Evaluate f(x) for every x in the domain to get the set of outputs.
The range is the set of images; the codomain is the declared target set B.

worked_examples.question: Find the domain and range of f(x) = x^2 where A = {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2}.
If f: A -> B with A = {1,2,3}, B = {a,b,c,d} and f = {(1,a),(2,c),(3,a)}, find the range.
worked_examples.solution: The images are a, c, a. So the range = {a, c}. Codomain = {a,b,c,d}.
worked_examples.answer: Range = {a, c}, Codomain = {a, b, c, d}.

exercises.question: Find the domain and range of f(x) = x + 1 where A = {0, 1, 2, 3}.
If f = {(1,5),(2,5),(3,5)} with codomain {5,6,7}, find the range.

concepts.title: Real Valued Functions
concepts.definition: A real valued function has its domain and codomain as subsets of the real numbers, including constant, identity, polynomial, rational, modulus, signum, and greatest integer functions.
concepts.formula: f: R -> R (or subsets of R); types: constant f(x)=c, identity f(x)=x, polynomial f(x)=a_n*x^n+..., rational f(x)=p(x)/q(x), modulus f(x)=|x|, signum f(x)=x/|x|, greatest integer f(x)=[x]
concepts.key_idea: Different standard functions map real numbers to real numbers following specific rules.
question_patterns: identify the type of the given real valued function
evaluate the constant or identity function at a point
find the value of the modulus or signum function
compute the greatest integer function value
Explain the method of Real Valued Functions.

solution_steps.explain: Determine whether the function is constant, identity, polynomial, rational, modulus, signum, or greatest integer.
Use the specific rule of the identified function type to evaluate at the given point.
Report the computed value along with the function type.

worked_examples.question: Evaluate the modulus function f(x) = |x| at x = -5.
worked_examples.solution: The modulus function returns the absolute value. f(-5) = |-5| = 5.

worked_examples.question: Evaluate the greatest integer function f(x) = [x] at x = 3.7.
worked_examples.solution: The greatest integer function returns the largest integer less than or equal to x. [3.7] = 3.

worked_examples.question: Evaluate the signum function f(x) = x/|x| at x = -4 (for x not equal to 0).
worked_examples.solution: Signum returns -1 for negative x. f(-4) = -4/|-4| = -4/4 = -1.

exercises.question: Evaluate the identity function f(x) = x at x = 7.
Evaluate the greatest integer function [x] at x = -2.3.

concepts.title: Graphs of Functions
concepts.definition: The graph of a function f is the set of all points (x, f(x)) in the Cartesian plane, where x ranges over the domain of f.
concepts.formula: Graph = {(x, y) : y = f(x), x in domain}
concepts.key_idea: Each x value corresponds to exactly one y value on the graph, reflecting the function property.
question_patterns: sketch the graph of the given function
identify the function from its graph
plot the points of the function
describe the shape of the graph of f
Explain the method of Graphs of Functions.

solution_steps.explain: Evaluate f(x) at several representative x values to get points (x, f(x)).
Mark each computed point on the Cartesian plane.
Join the points smoothly following the function rule to obtain the graph.

worked_examples.question: Sketch the graph of f(x) = x for x in {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2}.
worked_examples.solution: Compute points: (-2,-2), (-1,-1), (0,0), (1,1), (2,2). Plot and join them to get a straight line through the origin.
worked_examples.answer: The graph is a straight line through the origin with slope 1.

worked_examples.question: Sketch the graph of f(x) = |x| for x in {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2}.
worked_examples.solution: Compute points: (-2,2), (-1,1), (0,0), (1,1), (2,2). Plot and join to get a V-shaped graph.
worked_examples.answer: The graph is a V-shape with vertex at the origin.

exercises.question: Sketch the graph of the constant function f(x) = 3.
Identify the function whose graph is a V-shape with vertex at the origin.

concepts.title: Sum, Difference, Product, Quotient of Functions
concepts.definition: Given two real valued functions f and g with the same domain, their sum, difference, product, and quotient are defined pointwise as (f+g)(x)=f(x)+g(x), (f-g)(x)=f(x)-g(x), (fg)(x)=f(x)*g(x), and (f/g)(x)=f(x)/g(x) where g(x) is not zero.
concepts.key_idea: Arithmetic operations on functions are performed point by point over the shared domain.
question_patterns: find the sum of the functions f and g
compute the difference f - g at the given point
find the product of the two functions
evaluate the quotient f/g at x
Explain the method of Sum, Difference, Product, Quotient of Functions.

solution_steps.explain: Compute f(x) and g(x) at the given value of x.
Perform the required arithmetic operation (sum, difference, product, or quotient) on the two values.
Report the computed value, ensuring the denominator is non-zero for division.

worked_examples.question: If f(x) = x^2 and g(x) = 2x, find (f + g)(x) and evaluate at x = 3.
If f(x) = x^2 and g(x) = x + 1, find (f/g)(x) and evaluate at x = 2.

exercises.question: If f(x) = x and g(x) = x^2, find (fg)(x) at x = 4.
If f(x) = x^2 and g(x) = x, find (f - g)(x) at x = 5.
